newsitem.title: USA: Oxford reorganizes, changes specialty care.
newsitem.headline: Oxford reorganizes, changes specialty care.

text.p: Oxford Health Plans on Tuesday announced a restructuring of health care delivery system which includes a revamping of specialty care.
Under its new model, specialty care will be handled on a case-based approach that Oxford says emphasizes "healing and solutions."

In nine specialty areas the company said it is organizing teams of physicians, hospitals, therapists and other professionals who will be responsible for a patient's medical treatment from initial diagnosis to the conclusion of care.
Oxford shares were up 1-3/4 at 63-1/4 in Nasdaq trade.
A "performance profile" will be created for each team to allow consumers to compare success rates for the procedures they are preparing to undergo, said the company.
More than 200 specialty care teams have already been formed and the company expects 500 more care teams will form in 1997.

Oxford said it has also created the country's first credentialed alternative medicine network, with roughly 1,500 acupuncturists, chiropractors, massage therapists, yoga instructors, nutritionists and others.

Other changes include assigning a personal service agent to each member to minimize administrative hassle creating 24-hour telephone and on-line access to improve convenience; and expanding choice of providers.
